General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Hugging Face ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1389 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Predicting end-to-end fine-tuning time on shared GPU clusters, from 272 production runs.
  • It has been revealed that A preview of our upcoming paper, Predicting End-to-End Fine-Tuning Time for Generative Language Models.
  • GPUs are among the most expensive and scarcest resources in AI today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Predicting end-to-end fine-tuning time on shared GPU clusters, from 272 production runs.

It has been revealed that A preview of our upcoming paper, Predicting End-to-End Fine-Tuning Time for Generative Language Models. The full version will be on arXiv soon.

GPUs are among the most expensive and scarcest resources in AI today. Anyone running a shared cluster has to decide, every day, which jobs go on which GPUs and in what order. That initiative is only as good as the estimate of how long each job will take. When a job finishes hours early, GPUs sit idle until the next one is dispatched. When it runs hours late, everything queued behind it slips, experiments wait and delivery dates move.

Better duration estimates turn this into planning instead of guesswork: what runs, when, and on how many GPUs, with less idle capacity in between. Yet the estimate most teams use is a back-of-the-envelope FLOP calculation. It says nine hours, and the job finishes the next afternoon.

We wanted to know how far off that math really is, and whether we could do better before a job is even dispatched. So we took 272 real supervised fine-tuning (SFT) jobs from our production pool of NVIDIA H200 GPUs, about 7,382 GPU-hours in total, and compared analytical estimates against learned predictors.

According to recent reports, the short version: the usual FLOP-based estimate explains little of what we observed (R² = 0.31, MAE 12.41 h). A CatBoost regressor that only sees information available before dispatch reaches R² = 0.98, with a mean absolute error of 1.71 h and a median error of 0.51 h in 5-fold cross-validation. The gap comes from two things a closed-form estimate cannot do. The regressor sees more training-specific signals, such as evaluation cadence, checkpoint policy, per-GPU load and fine-tuning regime, and it learns the nonlinear interactions between them from past runs.

According to recent reports, for a dense Transformer, training costs roughly 6·P·D floating-point operations, where P is the parameter count and D the number of training tokens. Divide that by what your GPUs can deliver and you get a training-loop time:.

Here N_GPU is the number of GPUs, FLOPS_peak is the peak throughput of one GPU from its spec sheet, and MFU (Model FLOPs Utilization) is the fraction of that peak the training actually achieves. Real jobs never run at peak because of memory traffic, communication and kernel inefficiencies, so MFU typically sits somewhere between 30% and 60%, and the right value for a given job is not known in advance.

Sources indicate that this is a good description of the optimization loop. A job is more than its loop, though. Before the first step there is environment setup, model download and loading, and tokenization. During training there are periodic evaluations and checkpoint uploads. At the end, the final model goes to object storage. On a multi-tenant cluster, all of it competes with other jobs for network and storage I/O.

These overheads depend on configuration, and they do not scale neatly with workload or GPU count. Two jobs with the same nominal compute can finish hours apart.

To keep the comparison fair, the FLOP baseline we test counts the scheduled evaluation tokens as well as the training tokens, and we sweep MFU over a wide range.

We treat end-to-end duration as a supervised regression problem. Given a feature vector built from the job configuration and model metadata, predict the wall-clock time between the moment the job gets its GPUs and the moment it is done. Queue time is excluded.

Two design choices shaped the work:.

In a recent development, we compared Linear Regression, Ridge, XGBoost and CatBoost. Feature selection combined correlation filtering, mutual information and permutation importance across 18 candidate feature sets, followed by a grid search with MAE as the criterion. The final CatBoost model uses 24 features.

Industry observers note that distribution of end-to-end duration across the 272 runs. Mean 23.43 h, median 15.29 h.

All numbers come from stratified 5-fold cross-validation. The first four rows are analytical and involve no fitting.

No single MFU value fixes the FLOP baseline. We swept MFU from 0.25 to 0.65. The best setting, 30%, still leaves a mean error above 12 hours on jobs that last 23 hours on average.

Sources indicate that A more detailed analytical model does not close the gap. As a second baseline we took Calculon (Isaev et al., SC '23), an analytical performance model for LLM training from prior work. It builds an explicit layer graph and accounts for compute, memory traffic and inter-device communication. We extended the public implementation to cover LoRA, grouped-query attention, fused attention, bfloat16 and SwiGLU. Its estimates still correspond to a median of only 11% of the observed wall-clock time. That claims nothing against Calculon as a step-level tool, which is what it was designed for. It reveals how much of a production job happens outside the optimization step.

Linear models help, and then stall. Ridge brings MAE down to 7.23 h. The relationship between configuration and duration is not well captured by a purely linear model.

Gradient boosting does the heavy lifting. CatBoost and XGBoost land within one standard deviation of each other on every metric. We carry CatBoost forward because it has the lowest mean error across the board.

Industry observers note that catBoost's feature importance concentrates in a handful of features. Model and workload variables are there, as expected, but so are evaluation and checkpoint variables. num_eval_data, the total number of samples processed in evaluation over the life of the job, ranks first, followed by num_trainable_params, batch_eval_size_percent, num_all_params and num_gpus*batch_train_percent, with num_params_saved close behind. SHAP values tell the same story: high evaluation volume consistently pushes the predicted time up, while trainable parameter count has a nonlinear effect that only becomes large for the biggest models.

Mean feature importance of the CatBoost model across folds (PredictionValuesChange).

Feature importance is not a causal claim. Still, the pattern lines up with how a job is actually spent. How often you evaluate, how large the evaluation set is and how many checkpoints you persist all shape the wall-clock time, alongside model and dataset scale. These are choices people often make by habit when writing a training config.

One caveat on reading the plots: larger GPU allocations show positive contributions to predicted time. In our data, bigger allocations go with bigger jobs, so num_gpus acts partly as a proxy for job scale. It does not mean adding GPUs makes a job slower.

According to recent reports, looking at all 272 out-of-fold predictions, the median absolute error is 0.51 h. 80% of predictions are within 2.20 h and 90% are within 4.31 h. Broken down by job duration:.

Up to 60 hours, the median error stays at about one hour or less. The long tail is where the model struggles, and with only 13 runs above 60 hours we read that as a data limitation.

It has been revealed that out-of-fold absolute error against real duration, colored by duration range. Errors stay low up to 60 h and widen in the sparse tail.

According to recent reports, more data should still help. On a fixed 20% holdout, MAE drops from 1.63 h to 1.50 h when going from 85% to 100% of the training partition, with no clear plateau.

In practice, the predictor gives a scheduler a duration it can plan around before a job starts: which jobs to run together, when GPUs will free up, and whether a run will finish in time for its deadline.

Recent findings suggest that what does transfer is the method: overhead-aware features, multicollinearity-aware selection and the comparison protocol. The full paper will report the feature formulas, the selection procedure, the search spaces and the final hyperparameters in full, so the pipeline can be rebuilt on any execution-log dataset with a similar structure.

Next on our list: hardware-specific descriptors and validation on other GPU types, transfer learning for configurations with few observations, other training objectives, and more data on long runs.

The full paper is coming to arXiv soon. Follow the Dharma-AI organization on Hugging Face to be notified when it is out, and leave your questions in the comments below. We would like to hear how you estimate job duration on your own clusters.

Recent findings suggest that we have six apps of our own on the Solana dApp Store. Most of them started as web apps. Wrapping a web app into an Android app is now the easy part: Solana Mobile ships a free tool that does it in one command. What takes the time is everything that behaves differently once your site runs inside an app on a real Seeker. This post is the list we wish we'd had.

Solana Mobile's CLI builds a WebView shell around your site and signs an APK:.

init reads your web manifest for the name and icons and creates a signing keystore if you don't have one. build produces app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk. Solana Mobile now recommends this WebView shell over a Trusted Web Activity (the older Bubblewrap route): the shell needs no Digital Asset Links setup, and it handles Solana wallet requests natively, while browser network restrictions can break wallet connections inside a TWA.

If your app uses Mobile Wallet Adapter through @solana-mobile/wallet-standard-mobile, update it to 0.5.1 or later so it detects the shell.

So far, so quick. We tried it on a live dApp that offers Google sign-in, and on a Seeker it loaded perfectly. Then we tapped "Continue with Google".

In the shell, any link outside your app's own host opens in the system browser. That is the right default: it keeps unknown sites out of your app. But a Google sign-in is exactly such a link. What we saw on a Seeker:.

Sources indicate that you can't fix this by keeping the Google page inside the WebView: Google blocks its sign-in in embedded WebViews. The fixes that work:.

If your web app only offers Google and e-mail, test this first. It's the difference between a working app and one that loses every Google user at the door.

The same rule applies to window.open and target="_blank". Pay-with-card widgets, on-ramps, "share on X" buttons and help-desk chats often open that way. Some of that is fine (a share link should open X). Some isn't: a payment window that completes in Chrome leaves your app not knowing it happened. Go through every flow that opens something and decide: in the app, or out with a way back.

In a recent development, wallet behaviour is the part desktop testing can't show. On a Seeker, check:.

In a recent development, this is the work we do for other teams: the wrap, the sign-in and wallet fixes, real-device testing, the store listing and help through the publisher portal, published under your own account. Prices start at US$750; see our services page.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that today we are releasing DaisyRose-27B, RadixArk’s first model, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning using Miles.
  • The model retains Qwen3.8-27B’s architecture, tokenizer, chat template, image understanding, and 256K-token context window.
  • Industry observers note that we recommend serving DaisyRose-27B with SGLang and DSpark speculative decoding.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that today we are releasing DaisyRose-27B, RadixArk’s first model, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning using Miles. We trained it on long-horizon agent tasks with sessions up to 1M tokens, with just 1,200 curated tasks in 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs. DaisyRose-27B improves Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 from 5.6% to 12.0%. Beyond Terminal-Bench 4.1, it also delivers gains on a variety of other reasoning, instruction following, and coding benchmarks.

The checkpoints are available under Apache 2.0:.

The model retains Qwen3.8-27B’s architecture, tokenizer, chat template, image understanding, and 256K-token context window. The longer training sessions use harness summarization to span multiple trajectories. See the model card for model properties and inference settings.

Industry observers note that we recommend serving DaisyRose-27B with SGLang and DSpark speculative decoding. The SGLang cookbook provides launch configurations for different GPUs and checkpoint formats.

After starting the server with the served model name DaisyRose-27B on port 30000, you can send a request using the OpenAI Python client:.

The model thinks before answering by default. Its reasoning is returned in reasoning_content, and its final answer in content. These settings follow the model card’s quickstart.

It has been revealed that daisyRose-27B scores higher than the original Qwen3.8-27B model on every benchmark above. The largest gain is on Terminal Bench 4.1, where pass@1 rises from 5.6% to 12.0%.

Industry observers note that scores use the higher of the BF16 and FP8 runs for each benchmark; the two differ by less than one point wherever both were evaluated. The model card includes comparison sources and evaluation settings.

Three parts of the training setup made this release possible: carefully designed tasks, an efficient training backend, and reliable sandboxes.

According to recent reports, we built the tasks in partnership with Eigent AI, starting from its large pool of tasks in machine learning, software engineering, science, and other fields. Together we built thousands of candidates. About 1,200 made it into the final training set.

We selected tasks using three criteria:.

It has been revealed that radixArk trained DaisyRose-27B with Miles, our open-source reinforcement learning framework for large-scale model post-training, in fully asynchronous mode: the agent keeps working while the model learns, and neither waits for the other. While 128 H200s run the inference on agent tasks, 16 more run the trainer and learn from the trajectories. After every step, the updated model goes out to the 128 GPUs that run the agent. The learning runs on our internal training backend, which is built for agent training: each step learns from a handful of very long sessions, some as long as 1M tokens, folded into multiple trajectories via harness summarization.

Sources indicate that 57% lower training cost. On this release, 37% of each GPU’s peak compute went into useful training work (model FLOPs utilization, or MFU) on our backend. The open-source trainer, built on Megatron, reached 16% on comparable runs. So the same training needs 57% less GPU time. The gain is even larger on mixture-of-experts models: 6.2× on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and more than 10× on the roughly 300B-parameter GLM-5.3-Flash.

According to recent reports, 2× faster end to end. Counting the time the agent spends on its tasks, the release run trained on about 16,800 tokens per second across its 144 GPUs. The open-source trainer reached about 8,300 on the same GPUs.

Stable over weeks. The release run trained for weeks on 144 H200s, 63,000 GPU-hours in total. From the first step to the last, its speed and efficiency held steady.

Sources indicate that every training step of the DaisyRose-27B release run on 144 H200s, plotted against total training time. Dashed lines: the open-source trainer on comparable runs.

Every training attempt runs in a sandbox: a fresh copy of the task’s environment where the agent runs commands, edits files, and is then graded.

Sources indicate that our service is built on the open-source AgentENV project, to which we also contribute fixes. Between mid-September and mid-November, it ran about 944,000 sandboxes for this project, with up to 1,566 running concurrently.

According to recent reports, the service grew from one machine to as many as 12. We shipped ten upgrades to it, nearly all while training was running. Across all nine weeks, 99% of sandbox creations succeeded; since late October, that figure has exceeded 99.95%.

In a recent development, cloud infrastructure costs for the project’s sandboxes were about 80% lower than running the same sandboxes with popular cloud sandbox providers. One way we keep costs down is to let each sandbox’s memory allocation grow and shrink with its actual usage, allowing more sandboxes to share each machine.

Download DaisyRose-27B, follow the SGLang serving guide, or use Miles to train your own agents.

We’d like to hear how DaisyRose-27B performs on your tasks, including where it falls short. Share your setup and results in the model’s Community tab.

We thank Eigent AI for working closely with us on training data, and the Qwen team for creating Qwen3.8-27B. We also thank the Miles and SGLang communities, along with other open-source projects including slime, AgentENV, and Harbor.

  • Glama scores each tool's definition, not your marketing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ripSeek, one of our products, has a remote MCP server: AI apps such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor can ask it about Collector Crypt card packs (odds, the most valuable cards in each pack, recent pulls) and get live answers. Within a day of publishing, it was in the official MCP Registry and on Glama, where it scored A (3.9 out of 5) on tool quality, with a healthy status. Here is what mattered.

Glama scores each tool's definition, not your marketing. Its criteria are published as the Tool Definition Quality Score (TDQS); the top grade is A, from 3.5 up. The descriptions that score well, and that agents actually pick correctly, follow one pattern:.

It has been revealed that shows one Rare or Epic card that is in a pack pool right now: name, insured value, picture, and every pack it can come from with that pack's price and the chance per pack of pulling this exact card. Use it after search_cards, passing the nft field of a result; use search_cards when you only have a card name. Read-only; fails with a clear message if the card has just been pulled.

Industry observers note that glama's first review also flagged gaps in coverage, not just wording. It suggested making one tool's output clearer and adding a way to look up a single card; we added get_card and filters to list_recent_pulls. Then we rewrote all six descriptions against the pattern above.

When a tool can't answer, return a normal result with isError: true and a sentence the model can act on (for example "There's no pack with the code pokemon_5. Call list_packs to see the codes."), not a protocol error. The agent reads it, fixes its call and tries again, instead of giving up.

In a recent development, if you already have a public API, an MCP server is mostly a translation job: pick the 5 to 10 things people actually ask your product, write each as a tool with the pattern above, keep it read-only to start, and publish it under your own domain before someone else wraps your API under theirs. There are already hundreds of unofficial servers in the registry built on other companies' APIs.

We build these for other teams: on your existing API, on your own domain, listed in the registry and the main directories, from US$500. See our services page.

The pattern is open source as a template you can deploy in minutes: mcp-worker-template.

CVE-2026-77380: CVE-2026-77380: Server-Side Request Forgery via Unchecked Redirects in Bolt CMS

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (161 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dev

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vulnerability ID: CVE-2026-77380 CVSS Score: 5.2 Published: 2026-11-20.
  • Bolt CMS prior to version 6.1.5 is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in its asynchronous URL upload and media embed endpoints.
  • Authenticated consumers with ROLE_EDITOR permissions in Bolt CMS (< 6.1.5) can bypass URL safety checks on the /bolt/async/upload-url and /bolt/async/embed endpoints by supplying a public URL that redirects to internal or link-local IP addresses, resulting in Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vulnerability ID: CVE-2026-77380 CVSS Score: 5.2 Published: 2026-11-20.

Bolt CMS prior to version 6.1.5 is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in its asynchronous URL upload and media embed endpoints. While the application validates the initial user-supplied URL against internal network ranges using UrlSafetyChecker, the underlying HTTP transport libraries automatically follow HTTP 3xx redirects and HTML meta refresh directives without re-validating the target destinations. An authenticated user with editor privileges can exploit this discrepancy via an open redirector or DNS rebinding to access internal network resources and cloud metadata services.

Authenticated consumers with ROLE_EDITOR permissions in Bolt CMS (< 6.1.5) can bypass URL safety checks on the /bolt/async/upload-url and /bolt/async/embed endpoints by supplying a public URL that redirects to internal or link-local IP addresses, resulting in Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918).

fix(security): re-validate every hop when fetching remote URLs.

Read the full report for CVE-2026-77380 on our website for more details including interactive diagrams and full exploit analysis.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension.

Industry observers note that ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The firm was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Direct Comparisons: Ahrefs vs SEMrush.

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

In a recent development, ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

You'll also find some other options like.

Sources indicate that both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

In a recent development, if you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

It has been revealed that let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

Recent findings suggest that the Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Sources indicate that rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:.

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a upcoming project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:.

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Forget Expensive Ribeye: A Cheaper Cut For Delicious Beef Stroganoff

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that indulgently and immensely comforting, beef stroganoff is one of those low-effort meals you make when you just want to feel good.
  • It has been revealed that while it may not satisfy the purist, and might even horrify a Russian (the dish's country of origin), we'd argue that ground beef is a worthy alternative to any traditional whole cut of steak.
  • Another reason ground beef works so well here is its cooking time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that indulgently and immensely comforting, beef stroganoff is one of those low-effort meals you make when you just want to feel good. But one thing that might not lift your spirits is the price. Classic stroganoff starts off with strips of thinly sliced beef, with cuts like ribeye being among the best picks. We're not here to fault ribeye, which has earned its price for a reason, but if you want to knock a few dollars off your next batch, try swapping in ground beef instead.

It has been revealed that while it may not satisfy the purist, and might even horrify a Russian (the dish's country of origin), we'd argue that ground beef is a worthy alternative to any traditional whole cut of steak. The texture is bound to be different, and you'll need to adjust how you cook it, but good-quality ground beef still has the rich, beefy flavor that pairs so well with the tang of sour cream, earthy mushrooms, and the sweet depth of cooked-down onions, all at a significantly lower cost.

Another reason ground beef works so well here is its cooking time. Traditional beef stroganoff relies on expensive cuts that are prized for their tenderness and quick-cooking nature. Cheaper, tougher cuts like chuck or round usually need hours of braising to soften, which doesn't suit a dish that's meant to come together quickly. Ground beef, however, is often made from those same economical cuts, and the grinding process does all the tenderizing mechanically. That means you're getting all that mouthwatering flavor without the waiting, guaranteeing a tasty, Boomer-approved meal.

In a recent development, if you make the switch from ribeye to ground beef, you'll want to do a few things differently. First, check out the numbers on your ground beef packaging. You're looking for a blend that doesn't shy away from fat, something like an 80-to-20 lean-to-fat ratio, or even 70-to-30. Like ribeye, these fattier blends are packed with rich flavor, and the fat that'll render out will elevate the sauce, just in a different format. Go any leaner and you risk dry, chewy beef pebbles floating in your sauce.

With ribeye, standard practice is to slice the beef ultra-thin, give it a quick sear, then let it simmer in the sauce for a few minutes. The process for ground beef is similar, albeit with a few caveats. For starters, there's no slicing, so you're already saving time. Like ribeye, you want to get the meat nicely browned. Our personal advice is to add the beef to the pan in small handfuls and flatten each one with the back of a spoon, which allows it to brown without overcrowding the pan.

According to recent reports, remove the beef from the pan once it's seared, which isn't usually done with ribeye. Even in a fattier blend, ground beef has far more exposed surface area than your average slice of steak, so it risks drying out if it's left to simmer for too long. For the most tender results, build your sauce first, then add the beef back in and stir once you're just about ready to serve. Don't worry about the flavors not melding, since the fat and fond left behind from searing will be doing most of the heavy lifting.

You might not expect it, but sandwich chains are holding it down when it comes to Italian subs. Of course, there is no denying the appeal of a small, locally owned shop, but there are many reasons why you might opt instead to head into a chain to get your Italian hoagie fix, the most obvious of which is proximity. But there is also the fact that some chains just make darn good food. Food Republic did its research and compiled a list of the best chain Italian subs based on customer reviews, and each entry brings its own unique flavor to the table. But only one, the No. 13 Original Italian from Jersey Mike's, can claim to be the best old-school version of this particular sub.

"They do it right," one Reddit user stated, referencing the Original Italian. They continued by stating that if they had a classic Italian deli near them, they'd go there, but since they don't, "it's Jersey Mike's without question." Another user in that same thread agreed, writing, "I love this sub and am always a little amazed [it comes from] a chain" and not, presumably, from a traditional deli. And over on Google, a reviewer shared that the Original Italian reminded them of a sub they'd had during their childhood and expressed their gratitude that "there is a place that can make a real Italian hero like the old days.".

Recent findings suggest that it's worth noting that an old-school-style Italian sub owes it all to the Italian immigrants who populated this country throughout the 19th and 20th centuries. There are a few stories about how the hoagie came to be, including one based in Philadelphia (where it's the official sandwich of the city) involving shipyard workers and their distinctive lunches. There is another version that describes how Giovanna Amato sold filling sandwiches to dockworkers in Maine. Whatever its origins, the classic Italian sub came to be characterized by Italian meats and cheeses, a variety of fresh, crisp vegetables, a savory dressing, and an oily, vinegary drizzle.

Recent findings suggest that jersey Mike's Original Italian proves a chain can still honor those old-school roots. It checks every box, from five different Italian meats to provolone cheese to the default setting, Mike's Way, which includes onions, lettuce sliced super-thin, and tomatoes, as well as red wine vinegar and an olive oil blend, plus two impactful seasonings: salt and oregano.

But of course, Jersey Mike's serves 21st-century customers who like having options, so the sandwich, in addition to scratching an old-school itch, can also serve as a jumping-off point for some. You might, for example, upgrade your Original Italian sub by choosing the rosemary parmesan bread instead of plain white. There are a number of additional toppings available as well, such as jalapeño peppers, dill pickles, and hot chopped pepper relish.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s like your computer’s hard drive.
  • Industry observers note that blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

Recent findings suggest that it’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Industry observers note that blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

In a recent development, A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:.

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Sources indicate that blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more swiftly than ever.

It has been revealed that even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

According to recent reports, blockchain already being adopted by some significant-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Recent findings suggest that tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Recent findings suggest that blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Sources indicate that blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Recent findings suggest that have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a firm's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Recent findings suggest that blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Industry observers note that yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of people constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

According to recent reports, coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

According to recent reports, blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency.

In a recent development, generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. Skip Gruyère: This Norwegian Cheese Boasts Nutty Flavor & Fewer Calories

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that cheese is one of life's greatest pleasures, but no two varieties are quite the same. Knowing your way around your mozzarella and parmesan is a useful skill that won't just impress your dinner guests but will also transform the way you use cheese in the kitchen. Take Gruyère, for example. If, say, a French onion soup recipe calls for it, and you've had no luck finding it at the store, any cheese connoisseur will tell you that Norwegian Jarlsberg makes an excellent substitute. The two share a similar nutty flavor and melt beautifully, with Jarlsberg also serving a lower-calorie option.

Recent findings suggest that jarlsberg is instantly recognizable thanks to its large, round holes, and while traditional Swiss Gruyère might lack these holes, it matches Jarlsberg's intensely nutty flavor — although how the two cheeses develop their respective flavors is very different. Jarlsberg gets it from a proprietary bacterial culture called Propionibacterium shermanii, a sub-sect of Propionibacterium freudenreichii. During fermentation, this culture consumes lactic acid to produce propionic acid and carbon dioxide. The acid contributes to the cheese's nutty profile, while the carbon dioxide becomes trapped in the cheese, creating those large holes. Gruyère takes a different approach, developing its signature flavor through a combination of factors, including the unique composition of the high-altitude Alpine milk, its bacterial cultures, and a longer aging process.

Recent findings suggest that despite sharing a similar taste, their nutritional profiles tell a different story. Jarlsberg contains around 100 calories per ounce, compared with up to 120 calories for Gruyère. That's a modest saving of 20 calories per ounce, which can swiftly add up if you're using a generous amount in a grilled cheese or fondue. So if you're looking for a slightly lighter alternative to Gruyère without sacrificing flavor, Jarlsberg makes for a wonderful swap.

As is the case with Gruyère, one of Jarlsberg's biggest selling points is its versatility. You can always enjoy it as is, pairing it with grapes, crackers, and cold cuts as part of an elegantly presented charcuterie board, or keep things simple and serve it alongside a glass of wine; Jarlsberg goes particularly well with chardonnay and sweet rieslings, as well as low-tannin reds like pinot noir. While there are plenty of ways to enjoy the cheese without cooking it, we think the best way to get the most out of Jarlsberg is to take advantage of its meltability.

Jarlsberg's flavor is comparatively milder than that of sharper Gruyère, making it an excellent substitute if you're after a nutty, creamy cheese that won't overpower everything else, which makes it a great contender for a grilled cheese. If you still want some of Gruyère's intensity, simply combine the two. Their complementary flavor profiles mean neither cheese should overpower the other, giving you a nutty filling with plenty of depth. In a nod to Jarlsberg's Norwegian roots, add in some fresh dill, pickles, and a generous helping of cold-smoked salmon for a Scandi-inspired twist.

Another great way to put Jarlsberg to work is as a pizza topping. Its mild, buttery flavor and excellent meltability make it an obvious fit. Rather than tomato sauce, pair it with mushrooms, caramelized onions, and fresh thyme to let the cheese shine. If white pizza isn't your thing, swap the dough for Danish rye bread to create your own smørbrød, a charming Scandinavian open-faced sandwich. Simply take the buttered bread and add your toppings of choice, layer the Jarlsberg on top, then blast it in the broiler until creamy and gooey.

Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

📅 01 Jun 2022 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Blogspot

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are lots of questions floating around about how affiliate marketing works, what to do and what not to do when it comes to setting up a business.
  • Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies.
  • In a recent development, an affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are lots of questions floating around about how affiliate marketing works, what to do and what not to do when it comes to setting up a business. With so much uncertainty surrounding both personal and business aspects of affiliate marketing. In this post, we will answer the most frequently asked question about affiliate marketing1. What is affiliate marketing? Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!2. What is an affiliate program? An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.3. What is an affiliate network and how do affiliate networks make money? Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers. Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.4. What's the difference between affiliate marketing and dropshipping? Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands. 5. Can affiliate marketing and performance marketing be considered the same thing? Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action. 6. Is it possible to promote affiliate offers on mobile devices? Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile consumers by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.7. Where do I find qualified publishers? The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.8. What is an affiliate disclosure statement? An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases. 9. Does social media activity play a significant role in affiliate marketing? Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.10. What is a super affiliate? A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program. Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.11. How do we track publisher sales activity? Publishers can be identified by their publisher ID, which is used in tracking cookies to determine which publishers generate sales. The activity is then viewed within a network's dashboard. 12. Could we set up an affiliate program in multiple countries? Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.13. How can affiliate marketing help my business?Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways: It allows you to save time and money on marketing, which frees you up to focus on other aspects of your business. You get access to friendly marketers who are eager to help you succeed. It also helps you to promote your products by sharing links and banners with a latest audience. It offers high ROI(Return on investment) and is cost-effective. 14. How do I find quality publishers? One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.15. How Can we Promote Affiliate Links? Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:A website or blogThrough email marketing and newsletterSocial media, like Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter. Leave a comment on blogs or forums.Write an e-book or other digital product.Youtube 16. Do you have to pay to sign up for an affiliate program? To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.17. What is a commission rate? Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.Who manages your affiliate program? Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.18. What is a cookie? Cookies are small pieces of data that work with web browsers to store information such as user preferences, login or registration data, and shopping cart contents. When someone clicks on your affiliate link, a cookie is placed on the user's computer or mobile device. That cookie is used to remember the link or ad that the visitor clicked on. Even if the user leaves your site and comes back a week later to make a purchase, you will still get credit for the sale and receive a commission it depends on the site cookies duration19. How long do cookies last? The merchant determines the duration of a cookie, also known as its “cookie life.” The most common length for an affiliate program is 30 days. If someone clicks on your affiliate link, you’ll be paid a commission if they purchase within 30 days of the click.Final SayingMost new affiliates are eager to begin their affiliate marketing business. Unfortunately, there is a lot of bad information out there that can lead inexperienced affiliates astray. Hopefully, the answer to your question will provide clarity on how affiliate marketing works and the pitfalls you can avoid. Most importantly, keep in mind that success in affiliate marketing takes some time. Don't be discouraged if you're not immediately making sales or earning money. It takes most new affiliates months to make a full-time income.

  • Exact needs vary based on body type and medical history, but most adults need a minimum of about 0.36 grams of protein per pound of body weight daily.
  • In a recent development, if you use the best mayo for tuna salad — Kewpie, which is packed with MSG — you'll get an extra umami bomb.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tuna salad typically already comes with plenty of protein and flavor, but boosting these virtues can give you something even more delicious and nutritionally dense. This is especially true if you use boiled eggs, an easy-to-prepare ingredient that's highly compatible with whatever recipe you prefer.

Exact needs vary based on body type and medical history, but most adults need a minimum of about 0.36 grams of protein per pound of body weight daily. Beginning a recipe with canned tuna, which hovers around 22 grams of protein per 3-ounce serving, is a good start, but it can be better. A single boiled egg contains roughly 6 grams of protein and is rich in umami, no matter what texture you cook it to. The whites add a lovely, soft chew to counteract the density of fish meat, while the yolks themselves sort of disappear into the mayonnaise to boost its richness.

In a recent development, if you use the best mayo for tuna salad — Kewpie, which is packed with MSG — you'll get an extra umami bomb. Between the fish, egg, and MSG, you have all the makings of a hearty, satisfying meal, whether you eat it straight or heat it up in a melt. The end result is something that tastes more decadent than it does nutritious, full of velvety textures and rich flavors that make it seem like you spent quite a bit of time perfecting your recipe. Combine it all with minced veggies and pickles, and you get something comprehensively nourishing that's ready in a flash.

Eggs can be so much more than simply hard-boiled, so you've got plenty of options when it comes to the exact tastes and textures you want your tuna salad to have. Some bulk out a bowl, some focus on the sauce, and still others can add delightful fresh textures, but all are quite easy.

If you want something with an unobtrusive texture but a great amount of flavor, then boil your eggs for a jammy yolk. The runnier center diffuses through the mayonnaise, infusing it with flavor before it coats every piece of fish. If you're looking for something different, you can pan-fry hard-boiled eggs to crisp up the exteriors and add a touch of roasted flavor to a comparatively fresh and cool dish. If you use a flavored oil, like chili oil or one infused with herbs, this is an easy way to add new seasonings to the overall dish.

In a recent development, eggs can either introduce a dichotomy of textures or disappear into the meal, depending on your preference. Leaving your eggs whole or cut in half lets you spoon them into individual bites, preventing your meal from being too one-note. On the other hand, finely dicing them into crumbles is the best way to get their flavor into every nook, cranny, and ingredient. Using an egg slicer can give you the best of both worlds, creating thin slivers of white while the yolk dissolves into the mayonnaise.

Breaking: 7 Best Chain Restaurant Roast Beef Sandwiches, According To Customer Reviews

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that roast beef sandwiches are one of the most hearty and heartening meals there is.
  • In a recent development, and you won't be alone when you do.
  • Sources indicate that roy Rogers was once famed for its roast beef sandwiches, and today, people still line up for them whenever they get to visit one of the nearly 40 remaining locations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that roast beef sandwiches are one of the most hearty and heartening meals there is. That's why we think this comfort food deserves to be served year-round, not just on those brisk, rainy days when fall-apart-tender beef on a toasted baguette can be the most delicious way to warm up. Luckily, these chains' roast beef sandwiches are widely praised for their taste, texture, and consistency, so you can be sure you're getting a good-quality meal whenever you'd like to try one.

In a recent development, and you won't be alone when you do. According to the latest dedicated study on the subject, a 2019 survey by YouGov found that around 71% of adults across the country enjoyed roast beef sandwiches. That's one reason why the restaurants chosen for this list have the sandwich on the menu anytime you want it, and a few even overlap with the chains that have the best French dips. In the end, whatever place you choose to stop at will feed you well with homey, warm roast beef slices on toothsome bread.

Sources indicate that roy Rogers was once famed for its roast beef sandwiches, and today, people still line up for them whenever they get to visit one of the nearly 40 remaining locations. While it's been in business since the late 1960s, the chain has massively downscaled from its height of almost 650 stores in the 1990s. But the roast beef remains consistently delicious, thanks to the USDA Top Inside Round Roast Beef being slow-cooked for hours for maximum tenderness.

In a recent development, the sandwich has a hardcore fan base, who often say the beef here is tastier and juicier than other national competitors. One Reddit commenter said, "Roy's Roast beef is much better than Arby's. It actually tastes like real roast beef." Online reviewers suggest using the chain's barbecue and horseradish sauces to complete the experience. It helps that many of the remaining locations are in Maryland, where you can always grab some Baltimore tiger sauce for any leftovers.

It has been revealed that and customers are willing to accept the limited regional footprint of the restaurant, although they're still hoping for an overall comeback for the brand. Those lucky enough to have an open Roy Rogers nearby have reported being overjoyed at the discovery.

Sources indicate that arby's is a nostalgic favorite for many people for a reason – the perfectly textured and easy-to-chew beef. The global fast food chain began operations in 1964 but has since circled the globe with over 3,500 locations without forgetting that fact. That's why the roast beef Arby's uses has had the same four ingredients since it opened — beef, water, salt, and sodium phosphates. The meat is slow-cooked before being thinly sliced and added to a toasted sesame seed bun the diner can customize however they'd like.

People have called Arby's classic roast beef sandwiches their preferred fast food order, adding they rarely try anything else because the meal is so consistently good. Other fans have echoed that consistency is also what brings them back, with one person saying they've always enjoyed their items from the restaurant. A Facebook user posted about their first time trying Arby's, saying, "Tried Arby's roasted beef sandwich. It is pretty tender and flavorful. It's like a poor man's prime rib." And customers love that they can choose how much meat to have put on the sandwich, with some noting they've enjoyed half-pound versions, with and without cheddar sauce.

In a recent development, the smallest chain on this list is a Missouri powerhouse that's crossed over into Illinois. Even though that means most people will have to travel a bit to reach the nearest Lion's Choice, fans say the trip will be worth it. That's because the chain's roast beef sandwiches are made from the top round cut and are roasted in-house for freshness. Then there's the firm's proprietary blend of seasoning that's used to finish off the beef after it moves to the bun. The gluten-free mix helps set the meal apart from competitors, just like the secret roasting method does.

Sources indicate that fans of Lion's Choice are quick to recommend the establishment to newcomers, and those who've moved away look forward to the eatery being one of their first stops upon returning. Guests suggest getting extra seasoning on the beef, with some advising buyers to add cheese as well. The brand's horseradish sauce is also praised for being flavorful, although the beef is always the star of the show.

Recent findings suggest that black Bear Diner is an up-and-coming chain operating almost 170 locations across 14 states at the time of writing. Founded in 1995, the brand is dedicated to making comfort foods that taste as if they came straight from the best cook in the family's kitchen. The restaurant's Pot Roast Melt is certainly living up to that expectation. The meal is made with jack and cheddar cheeses, grilled onions, horseradish aioli, and slowly simmered pot roast. The sandwich also comes with au jus and is served on garlic- and Parmesan-crusted sourdough bread for a bit of crunch.

The melt gets consistent praise from customers, whether it's the diner's first time trying the sandwich or if they've come back just for another one. One Facebook user posted about the meal, saying, "Black Bear Diner knocked it out of the park with their Pot Roast Melt! Pot Roast, onion and cheesy goodness on grilled parmesan/garlic bread. On top of that – you get to dip it in au jus!" Others have called it yummy, delicious, and so good, cementing the elevated status of the sandwich for Black Bear Diner fans.

In a recent development, like Lion's Choice, Culver's is another Midwest favorite for beef sandwiches. But Culver's is a little different because it's one of the only fast food chains that serves shredded pot roast instead of sliced beef. That creates a major difference in the taste and texture of the premium chuck roast the brand uses, so it's no surprise that Culver's Pot Roast Sandwich is praised for its rich flavor and lack of fat. One person was so impressed with the meal that they made it their go-to item from the menu.

Other diners point out the generous size of the sandwich, as well as how juicy and tender the meat is. Fans suggest adding gravy and/or grilled onions to finish off the sandwich, but barbecue sauce is another popular way to add spice to the roast. Some people add Swiss cheese and mushrooms, too, although you might need to eat it rapidly to keep the bun intact.

It has been revealed that firehouse Subs is one of the largest fast food sandwich franchises in the U.S., with over 1,300 stores. It started in the mid-1990s and has always been dedicated to making filling meals that each diner could customize exactly as they'd like. The large menu includes hot and cold subs, as well as in-house sides and desserts. One of the most popular hot sandwiches is the Smokehouse Beef & Cheddar Brisket, which fans praise for its melty cheddar cheese, strong beefy flavor, and the incredibly tender brisket.

According to recent reports, people agree that Firehouse Subs is a pricier option than many other sandwich shops, but the quality of the ingredients and the generous portions make up for the higher cost. One Facebook user stated, "Trying Firehouse Subs for [the] first time. Large smokehouse beef and cheddar combo, with small fries. Pricier than Subway at $32.42, but bloody delicious!!" Others agree about the taste, saying the sandwich is one of their favorites and that they've had consistently good experiences eating one.

Industry observers note that portillo's is a Chicago-based chain that's best known for its Italian-style roast beef sandwiches, although there are several kinds of roast beef subs on the menu. Served either dipped in au jus or dry, the meaty Italian Beef Sandwiches have a nice kick of spice from the Italian peppers that come atop the layered protein. The meal is so sought after that the business ships kits nationwide to make the Italian beef sandwiches. The set comes with all the elements needed to re-create the meal at home, and it serves up to 10 people.

In a recent development, reviewers note the hot peppers that come on the sub add a spicy crunch that works nicely with the richness of the juicy meat. One Facebook user posted about the item, saying, "...I had a Portillo's beef yesterday with hot and sweet peppers and dipped twice. It was a pretty darn good beef sandwich.".

Like that Facebook poster, many fans prefer to have the sandwich dipped, saying the flavor is worth the extra napkins you'll need. Some people even make long drives just to visit the shop. And who could blame them? The hot beef Italian subs offer great taste and value for some of the most tender meat you'll find at any chain restaurant.

According to recent reports, to build a list of the best roast beef sandwiches, we first searched for chain restaurants with more than 24 locations that served the meal. We then looked through social media and message board posts and comments, user review sites, and professional reviews for each chain's roast beef. We ultimately chose the restaurants whose customers had praised the meal for its taste, value, and consistency across multiple platforms to be represented on this list.

Two Personality Traits Linked To A Sharper Mind

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How you respond to beauty may have more in common with your thinking skills than you realise.
  • How you respond to beauty may have more in common with your thinking skills than you realise.
  • Intellectual curiosity and an appreciation of beauty are both linked to stronger thinking skills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How you respond to beauty may have more in common with your thinking skills than you realise.

How you respond to beauty may have more in common with your thinking skills than you realise.

Intellectual curiosity and an appreciation of beauty are both linked to stronger thinking skills.

People with these qualities tend to perform better on tests of literacy, numeracy and problem-solving.

The findings suggest that a person’s interest in ideas and aesthetic experiences may offer clues to their cognitive abilities.

Curiosity could encourage people to seek out opportunities to learn, while stronger thinking skills could make exploring complex ideas more rewarding, with both processes reinforcing one another.

Intellectual curiosity involves enjoying ideas, wanting to understand things and being drawn to questions that require thought.

Aesthetic sensitivity describes an appreciation of art and beauty.

Both qualities belong to the broader personality trait of openness to experience, which captures how receptive people are to unfamiliar ideas and experiences.

However, openness also includes creative imagination, and this aspect showed no significant independent association with cognitive performance.

Imagination, curiosity and an appreciation of beauty may overlap in everyday life, but their relationships with thinking skills differ.

The conclusions come from an analysis of almost 68,000 people across 12 countries, including Canada, Germany, Italy and New Zealand.

They completed personality questionnaires alongside assessments of literacy, numeracy and the ability to solve problems as circumstances change.

Intellectual curiosity and aesthetic sensitivity were linked to better performance across all three assessments, even after accounting for other personality traits.

The connections between personality and cognitive skills also varied between countries.

Educational systems and cultural practices could help explain such differences, although the reasons remain uncertain.

Overall, the findings link both a desire to understand the world and an appreciation of its beauty with stronger thinking skills.

The study was published in the journal Large-scale Assessments in Education (Rammstedt et al., 2026).

Sources indicate that psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

📅 13 Jul 2022 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Blogspot

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry.
  • Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time.
  • Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers.

In a recent development, phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

In a recent development, when you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

In a recent development, acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include significant brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and organization-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool reveals you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

It has been revealed that yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

According to recent reports, albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, upcoming marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

  • Pat LaFrieda has built its reputation on providing quality beef and other meat products to some of the best restaurants in the country, and it has become famous for providing these eating establishments with specialty cuts and portions, its dry-aged beef, and its custom ground beef blends, including (and especially) Shake Shack's.

Shake Shack, which has come from humble beginnings as a hot dog cart in New York City, has built a loyal following of fans since it first transitioned to permanent kiosks in 2004. From the first, the emphasis of its food has been on the quality of its ingredients. That means cage-free eggs for its breakfast items, 100% beef for its hot dogs, all-natural chicken from cage-free birds, and some of the best Angus beef around, with no added hormones or antibiotics. Indeed, the beef that forms Shake Shack's burger patties is a cut above, a proprietary blend that involves both chuck and brisket, and a spokesperson from Shake Shack told Food Republic that meat is supplied by upscale wholesaler brand Pat LaFrieda Meat Purveyors.

Described as "one of our longest-standing supplier partners and our largest purveyor by volume," the spokesperson informed us that the source of the partnership harkens back to the founder's, Danny Meyer's, involvement in the NYC fine dining world (Meyer was the original owner of Eleven Madison Park). The collaboration is indicative of Shake Shack's commitment to quality: "Pat LaFrieda helps us deliver the Shake Shack burger our guests know and love, [which is] made with 100% Angus beef, our custom blend of brisket and chuck [has] no preservatives, fillers[,] or additives, always fresh, never frozen, and humanely raised and grazed.".

Pat LaFrieda has built its reputation on providing quality beef and other meat products to some of the best restaurants in the country, and it has become famous for providing these eating establishments with specialty cuts and portions, its dry-aged beef, and its custom ground beef blends, including (and especially) Shake Shack's. The grinders in its manufacturing plant in New Jersey are capable of making more than 150 different unique mixes of ground beef from a variety of cuts, and if you were to partner with the butcher for a restaurant, you could create your own unique recipe.

And it's benefits like that which has allowed Shake Shack to spread its wings beyond its regular burger menu (which Food Republic tried and ranked) and test out a Dry-Aged Beef Burger at one of its NYC locations. According to the organization's spokesperson, the limited-run burger (the last day to grab one was October 17, 2026) was "made with 35-day dry-aged beef for a deeper, more intense flavor," and it featured absolutely decadent caramelized shallot and a sauce made from bone marrow (as well as raw white onion to add a sharp note in contrast with all the richness), which were all served up on a milk bread bun dotted with black and white sesame seeds.

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (557 w)
