    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    The Best Chain Restaurant Grilled Reuben Melt, According To Customers

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (419 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It's hard to mess up a Reuben because the ingredients are so simple: corned beef, sliced thin, tangy sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and Thousand Island dressing (or Russian), all of which are sandwiched between two pieces of sturdy rye bread.
    • To that end, Food Republic did the legwork and created a list of the top Reubens you can order from a chain, from customers' perspectives, and one of the entries actually comes from Culver's.
    • Were you aware that Culver's even had a Grilled Reuben Melt on its menu?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's hard to mess up a Reuben because the ingredients are so simple: corned beef, sliced thin, tangy sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and Thousand Island dressing (or Russian), all of which are sandwiched between two pieces of sturdy rye bread. No matter where you get your Reuben from, it's safe to say there are typically no bad ones — just good, better, and best.

    To that end, Food Republic did the legwork and created a list of the top Reubens you can order from a chain, from customers' perspectives, and one of the entries actually comes from Culver's. The Midwestern favorite, better known for its unique ButterBurgers, apparently makes the best grilled version of the sandwich you can find.

    Were you aware that Culver's even had a Grilled Reuben Melt on its menu? Because for as many customers who sing its praises, there appear to be an equal number who didn't even know it was an option. But what an option it is; it's a classic version, with lightly toasted bread, piles of salty corned beef, and melty Swiss cheese made in Culver's home state of Wisconsin.

    One Reddit user shouted out the sandwich, writing that it "matches or beats some of the ones that I've had at many diners." Another commenter remarked that Culver's "slaps in general[,] but this goes hard for a fast food Reuben." Meanwhile, yet another Redditor called it "the best thing on the menu and the best [Reuben] I've ever had.".

    Recent findings suggest that one of the best things about Culver's menu is how customizable it is, and the Reuben is no different. Culver's maintains a fairly long list of toppings that you can add to your melt; one Reddit user claimed that "[grilled onions] and mushrooms are the easiest way to elevate the sandwiches," though keep in mind that you might have to request customizations in person because online ordering doesn't always have the option. You could also add raw onions for a sharper bite, lettuce for a little greenery, tomato for some extra umami flavor, and, for a small fee, some thick-cut bacon.

    Another user suggested adding a burger patty to the sandwich, calling the addition "incredible." Finally, if you're not a huge fan of rye, you could also swap it out for sourdough (the melt would then actually more closely resemble the best non-traditional chain restaurant Reuben, found at Schlotzsky's Deli), or opt for its Kaiser bun, brioche roll, gluten-free bun if you have a wheat allergy.

    #10695. Tech Report: 5 Types Of Brain-Affecting Drugs Still Prescribed Despite Safety Warnings

    Tech Report: 5 Types Of Brain-Affecting Drugs Still Prescribed Despite Safety Warnings

    📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (496 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Five drug groups carry warnings for older adults, yet prescribing remains highest among those with dementia.
    • Five drug groups carry warnings for older adults, yet prescribing remains highest among those with dementia.
    • One in four older Americans with dementia is prescribed potentially inappropriate medicines that affect the brain and nervous system.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Five drug groups carry warnings for older adults, yet prescribing remains highest among those with dementia.

    Five drug groups carry warnings for older adults, yet prescribing remains highest among those with dementia.

    One in four older Americans with dementia is prescribed potentially inappropriate medicines that affect the brain and nervous system.

    These drugs can increase the risk of confusion, falls and hospitalisation, particularly in people whose thinking and memory are already impaired.

    Despite decades of warnings, people with cognitive impairment were more likely to receive these prescriptions than those with normal cognition.

    The research examined five categories of medication flagged by prescribing guidelines for older adults:.

    Only antidepressants with strong anticholinergic properties were included in this category.

    Anticholinergic medicines block acetylcholine, a chemical messenger involved in memory, learning and concentration.

    Blocking its action can cause confusion and other unwanted effects, especially in older adults.

    Benzodiazepines, which may be prescribed for anxiety or sleep problems, can cause excessive drowsiness and increase the risk of falls.

    Some medicines also take longer to leave the body as people age, allowing their effects to persist or accumulate.

    The researchers analysed survey information linked to medical insurance records from almost 4,900 Americans aged 65 and over.

    They examined prescribing over nine years, counting prescriptions for at least four weeks’ supply.

    Around 17 percent of people with normal cognition received at least one potentially inappropriate prescription, compared with almost 22 percent of those with cognitive impairment without dementia.

    Among people with dementia, the proportion reached 25 percent.

    Across the older adults studied, prescribing fell from around 20 percent at the beginning of the study period to 16 percent at the end.

    Much of the decline reflected fewer prescriptions for benzodiazepines and Z-drug sleeping medicines.

    However, prescribing rates for the other three drug groups did not change significantly.

    By the final year, more than two-thirds of people receiving these potentially inappropriate prescriptions lacked a documented clinical reason for at least one of them.

    A potentially inappropriate medicine can still be justified when its expected benefits outweigh its risks.

    The practical question is whether each prescription remains suitable for the person taking it.

    Dr Annie Yang, the study’s first author, emphasised the importance of patients and carers reviewing these medicines with their physicians:.

    “While CNS-active prescriptions may be appropriate in some cases, it is key for older patients or their caregivers to work closely with their physicians to ensure that these medications are appropriate to their cases.

    When inappropriate, patients and their care teams should consider alternative treatments and consider whether it might be safe to taper or stop the medication.”.

    The study was published in JAMA (Yang et al., 2026).

    Sources indicate that psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean.

    #10691. 12 Powdered Gravy Mixes, Ranked Worst To Best

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (3021 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    12 Powdered Gravy Mixes, Ranked Worst To Best

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • Recent findings suggest that as most pro home chefs will tell you, making gravy from scratch isn't exactly rocket science.
    • Industry observers note that even so, the kind of store-bought gravy mix you choose matters — after all, anything you're planning to drown your meat and taters in had better be good.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Recent findings suggest that as most pro home chefs will tell you, making gravy from scratch isn't exactly rocket science. With the help of a little flour, butter, and broth, you could be on your way to a delicious gravy in just a few minutes. Still, there may be times when you simply aren't feeling up to it — whether you've had a rough week or are drowning in to-dos, packets of powdered gravy mix can prove a simple, flavorful fix.

    Industry observers note that even so, the kind of store-bought gravy mix you choose matters — after all, anything you're planning to drown your meat and taters in had better be good. That's why I decided to make it my mission to test some of the most popular powdered gravy options in my area in hopes of offering my honest opinion about which truly deserves a spot in your kitchen.

    Sources indicate that in the upcoming post, I'm giving a complete rundown of every store-bought powdered gravy mix I could find, including the pricing, size, and taste of each. Bear in mind that the details mentioned in this article are subject to change and that the gravy packet selection featured here may not be reflective of what's available in your area. With that, join me as I prepare, taste, and rank 12 store-bought powdered gravy mixes from worst to best.

    Prices are as of the date of publication and may vary based on region.

    Sources indicate that great Value Chicken Gravy Mix is a no-frills Walmart-branded product that is, surprisingly, one of the costlier options on the list when you consider its price per unit. Though tagged at only 92 cents per packet, each pack contains .87 ounces, meaning you'll pay roughly $1.06 per ounce of powdered gravy.

    Great Value Chicken Gravy Mix is prepared using the standard 1 cup of water per 1 packet of mix, and its ingredients include monosodium glutamate (otherwise known as "MSG"), which may pose a problem for gravy lovers who may be sensitive to the ingredient. I tore open the packet, and its unappetizing, artificial smell hit me right away. Once cooked, the mixture turned creamy and thick, but its color seemed unnatural, especially when compared to homemade. I gave it a hesitant taste, and nope, not good — Great Value Chicken Gravy Mix tasted like stale chicken and literally made me gag.

    Would I recommend purchasing Great Value Chicken Gravy Mix? No way. Not only does its bright yellow color not resemble any chicken gravy I've ever made, but the taste was barely tolerable. I'm sure you could try improving this store-bought gravy with Worcestershire sauce, but I say, if it's convenience you seek, there are other options more deserving of your coin than this one.

    In a recent development, I hate to have to rank yet another Great Value powdered gravy mix so close to the bottom of the list, but it simply cannot be helped. Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix is a bit cheaper than its chicken-flavored counterpart — expect to pay 78 cents per .87 ounces, which works out to around 89.7 cents per ounce of powdered gravy. Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix doesn't contain the MSG that the chicken flavor includes, but that doesn't mean I recommend purchasing it — like the former, it has a weird smell and taste that I simply can't get past.

    I prepared Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix according to the package directions and watched it bubble and simmer on the stove. The mix eventually turned the typical light brown color normally associated with turkey gravy and had an uber-thick consistency. I let it cool slightly before giving it a quick taste — sadly, it had the same stomach-churning qualities as the previous flavor. Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix tasted woefully artificial; in fact, the additives or chemicals present in the gravy were just about the only thing I could taste. Needless to say, I would never dish up Great Value Turkey Gravy Mix to guests at Thanksgiving — you'd be better off leaving not-so-Great Value picks like this one on the shelf.

    Before offering my opinion here, I have to be honest and say I'm not a person who prepares peppered gravy often. That remarked, I'm willing to bet Southeastern Mills Peppered Gravy Mix doesn't quite encapsulate its classic flavor the way other options do.

    Southeastern Mills Peppered Gravy Mix costs $1.22 per 2.75 ounces, with a unit price of 44.4 cents per ounce. As is typical for many peppered gravy mixes on the market, this packet contains a little more powdered gravy mix per pack than other varieties and flavors. Its preparation requires more water, too — you'll need 1 ¾ cups this time around versus the usual 1 cup.

    It has been revealed that southeastern Mills Peppered Gravy Mix tasted annoyingly bland, with a flavor very similar to what you'd get if you added black pepper to plain cream. Though thick, it had no richness of flavor, and I couldn't imagine it doing much to elevate anyone's sausage gravy. I flipped the packet over and was surprised by what I saw on the ingredient list: Palm oil and modified food starch were the first ingredients mentioned, which is hardly a good way to start a high-quality gravy, if you ask me. As I mentioned, I am by no means an expert in peppered gravy, but based on first impressions alone, I'd say skip this brand and opt for other, richer, more flavorful brands on the market.

    If you're surprised to see McCormick Brown Gravy Mix ranked lower on the list, join the club. I, for one, adore brown gravy, and with McCormick being one of the most popular gravy and seasoning brands on the market, I figured I'd be in for a real treat. Expect to pay 97 cents for .87 ounces of it, making each ounce cost roughly $1.12.

    When cooking up McCormick Brown Gravy Mix, I couldn't help but feel excited — its texture was thick and glossy, and the gravy had a deep brown hue that just screamed umami beef. It even had the savory, enticing aroma of a succulent pot roast, so imagine my surprise when I discovered the gravy tastes, quite literally, like nothing.

    That's right — McCormick Brown Gravy Mix features a flavor so weak I could barely taste anything at all. To think McCormick Brown Gravy Mix smelled and looked so great without delivering flavor even half of what was teased is mind-boggling. Needless to say, McCormick Brown Gravy Mix isn't worth the buy — I'd recommend picking up some beef broth and making your own simple brown gravy or choosing one of the higher-ranking varieties over this one.

    Industry observers note that though not the best out there, Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix is a dark horse in terms of taste and performance. The gravy comes sold in an .87-ounce pack and was priced at 83 cents, about 95 cents per ounce. It contains artificial ingredients along with a host of additives, but hey, if that kinda stuff doesn't bother you, feel free to ignore those stats.

    I went into my tasting of Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix with low expectations — almost every Amazon Grocery item I've sampled in the past left me underwhelmed. Much to my amazement, Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix held its own in terms of consistency and aroma — it was a bit thinner than a few other options on the list, yes, but still managed to be just thick enough. I also found its glossy deep brown appearance mesmerizing, and its smell rich and meaty, just the way a good brown gravy should be.

    Going in for a slurp, I didn't walk away disappointed — though the flavor was nowhere near as potent as its aroma, it was leaps and bounds better than McCormick. I could clearly taste its beefy notes, and its umami depth was decent overall. One thing I will say is that Amazon Grocery Brown Gravy Mix tastes slightly watered down; still, I think it will get you by if you're looking for a tasty, inexpensive brown gravy to crown your mashers.

    Recent findings suggest that pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix is pretty good; though not a peppered gravy kinda gal, I have an appreciation for this brand and would recommend it over Southeastern Mills any day. This mix comes in a 2.75-ounce packet, only this time, you'll need to add 2 cups of water instead of the 1 ¾ cups Southeastern Mills requires. Each packet costs $1.33, meaning you'll cop this powdered peppered gravy for about 48.4 cents per ounce.

    Recent findings suggest that when cooking up Pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix, the first thing I noticed was its golden hue. The yellowish tinge of the Pioneer-branded gravy made it more attractive than the stark white presentation of Southeastern Mills. It was just as thick as the former brand, if not thicker, though whether or not its flavor would prove better was yet to be seen.

    According to recent reports, so, how'd Pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix taste? Though I still consider its flavor mundane compared to traditional chicken or brown gravies, Pioneer Peppered Gravy Mix had more depth than Southeastern Mills. It's not listed in the ingredients, but there seemed to be a hint of butter flavor in the mixture — this deepened the taste and added complexity. All in all, if I were to grab a packet of peppered gravy for breakfast, this is the brand I'd get — not only does it look better, but its taste is pretty decent, too.

    According to recent reports, mcCormick Turkey Gravy Seasoning Mix wasn't too bad — it isn't something I'd choose over homemade gravy for Thanksgiving dinner, but it's good if you're in a pinch and want something cheap. The gravy comes sold in a .87-ounce packet for $1.63, and while this might not sound super expensive, it's actually a little pricier than others, at $1.87 per ounce.

    According to recent reports, mcCormick Turkey Gravy Seasoning Mix yields a light brown color I found fitting for turkey gravy — it certainly looked the part, featuring a medium-thick consistency and glossy appearance. McCormick Turkey Gravy Seasoning Mix has a poultry-like flavor that's pleasing but leans more chicken than turkey in my opinion. Nevertheless, I consider this turkey gravy option to be one of the punchier, more robust picks out there, and though I don't necessarily consider it holiday worthy, it might be good to have a packet or two in your pantry for days when you're low on time.

    In a recent development, fire & Smoke Society Substantial Sunday Brown Gravy Mix is a super unique option, and though I probably wouldn't buy it again, you might consider trying it if you're looking to sample something outside of the norm. The packaging here has the kind of aesthetic that makes you think it's fancy by looks alone — its price also stands out, at $1.72 per 1-ounce pack, working out to $1.72 per ounce. A quick scan of the ingredients reveals several surprises — though not a clean ingredient pick by any means, some additions — like cumin, chili powder, and even coffee — left me curious as to what kind of flavor I was in for.

    According to recent reports, I prepared the gravy as per its 1 cup to 1 packet instructions and immediately noticed a difference in its texture compared to the others. Fire & Smoke Society Big Sunday Brown Gravy Mix yields a thinner, silkier texture than most. Its aroma was totally unexpected, as it was more akin to grill spices than savory beef. After tasting Fire & Smoke Society's Big Sunday Brown Gravy Mix, I found myself torn — the taste wasn't gross, but didn't encompass the type of flavor I expect from a classic brown gravy.

    It has been revealed that is Fire & Smoke Society Massive Sunday Brown Gravy Mix good? Yes! Would I buy it again? Probably not. Blame it on my traditional taste buds, but for me, this powdered gravy mix is just OK.

    Industry observers note that is there a difference between country and peppered gravy? Apparently, there is, and as it stands, I prefer the former. Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning was a breath of fresh air flavor-wise, but I suppose that isn't surprising given I love practically anything that the Kinder brand produces. Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning was priced at $1.72 per 1.9 ounces at my local Walmart, working out to about 90.5 cents per ounce.

    Sources indicate that kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning was truly phenomenal in terms of taste and texture. First and foremost, the gravy recommends preparing it with 2 cups of milk, which automatically gave it a richer, sweeter finish. Once cooked, the gravy was thick and featured a stark white appearance flecked with tons of contrasting black pepper throughout.

    Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning tastes almost identical to creamy, buttery, garlicky mashed potatoes, no spuds needed. I'd imagine this would taste incredible paired with creamy taters, and I wouldn't hesitate to dish it up as a turkey topper during the holidays. As if things couldn't get better, Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning uses fairly clean ingredients, with nowhere near as much of the ick featured in other powdered gravy mixes on the list. With all things considered, Kinder's Classic Country Gravy Dry Seasoning is one of my favorite powdered gravy mixes on the market.

    Recent findings suggest that simply Organic Roasted Chicken Gravy Seasoning Mix costs $1.72 for .85 ounces making it one of the most expensive powdered gravy mixes on the market at $2.02 per ounce. It's the only gluten-free organic chicken option on the list, and I honestly didn't expect it to taste as good as it did. Not that I have anything against organic foods — I actually love them and find the use of minimal ingredients refreshing. Still, in the world of gravy, I guess I just didn't expect a natural option like this one to hold its own when pitted against others containing various flavor-boosting additives. Thankfully, this humble pick from Simply Organic proved me wrong.

    According to recent reports, simply Organic chicken gravy calls for the standard 1 cup of gravy packet seasoning per 1 cup of water. As it cooked, it began to take on a sauce-like consistency that was thick, glossy, and light brown. I gave it a taste and was floored — this organic pick boasted a flavor way better than any other store-bought chicken gravy I've tried.

    Sources indicate that simply Organic chicken gravy had a bold, savory, and garlicky flavor beautifully enhanced with prominent notes of celery seed. Thus, though expensive, you can rest assured that your money is going to good use — Simply Organic Roasted Chicken Gravy Seasoning Mix is a phenomenal replacement for homemade when you don't feel like whipping up chicken gravy on your own.

    Recent findings suggest that simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix is the only organic brown gravy on the list, and let me tell you, it did not disappoint. Unlike its chicken-flavored predecessor, Simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix is slightly cheaper, at 1 ounce for $1.72 ( $1.72 per ounce). Being the organic grab that it is, expect Simply Organic brown gravy to be non-GMO and free of artificial colors, flavors, and ingredients. One of its best attributes is its use of cornstarch rather than flour, as this makes it a great option for people looking to ditch wheat.

    Industry observers note that I was delighted to find Simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix packing so much flavor — after the previous brown gravy duds, I didn't have much hope that there was a truly good packaged option out there. In truth, Simply Organic's brown gravy is one of the most flavorful in its class — it was one of the few to truly capture the beefy, oniony savor I come to expect from a good homemade brown gravy.

    One thing to note is that Simply Organic brown gravy has a medium consistency and a color a lot lighter than others in its category. Still, Simply Organic Brown Gravy Seasoning Mix would make the perfect companion to roast beef or over creamy mashed potatoes, and I doubt anyone would be able to detect the difference between it and homemade.

    Yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy is unlike any other gravy I've tried — I had never sampled jalapeño gravy before, nor did I know it existed. Now that it's on my radar, in my cabinet it will stay. It's really that good, even if it is $2.50 per 2.82-ounce packet (89 cents per ounce)!

    Sources indicate that yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy contains no artificial flavors, which to me is pretty impressive. Though not gluten-free like the aforementioned Simply Organic picks, it does at least contain fewer additives while still managing to achieve unbelievably thick results. You only need to use 2 cups of water per packet to cash in on this irresistibly luscious golden gravy; its texture was so rich and smooth my mouth watered just at the sight of it.

    It has been revealed that aside from its tantalizing consistency, Yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy tastes incredible — I'd describe its flavor as similar to high-quality jalapeño nacho cheese, but with less emphasis on the cheese. It's quite spicy, and though not unbearably so, still isn't something I'd recommend offering to kids. All in all, Yellowstone Jalapeño Gravy is an amazing option I'd buy over and over again — try it on fried chicken cutlets, potatoes, stuffing, or hot sandwiches. Yum!

    The 12 powdered gravy mixes selected for this article were chosen based on availability in my area, with most sourced from Walmart and Amazon. Each gravy mix was ranked primarily based on texture and flavor, although other factors, like ingredients and pricing, were considered. As always, pricing and availability are subject to change.

    According to recent reports, from birthdays to holiday gatherings, a beautiful cake can be the star attraction and make an ordinary occasion feel extraordinary. Thanksgiving is right around the corner, and while pies are often the go-to dessert for this holiday, serving your guests something unexpected in the form of a cake can turn your dinner into a memorable feast, especially if they have multiple meals to attend. Sure, you can make one from scratch, but with all the activity and planning surrounding this holiday, you may just want to opt for something store-bought, and Costco offers the perfect solution.

    It has been revealed that the Costco bakery offers a huge range, from decadent layer cakes in crowd-pleasing flavors to rich cheesecakes — which aren't technically cakes, though we're including them here anyway. There are also some Italian-style specialties, a truly seasonal option, and one flourless chocolate cake that will bring a touch of luxury to your table.

    Keep in mind that the wholesale club requires a membership for customers to shop there. If you're not already a member, this list of cakes may convince you to join. Just remember that prices and availability may vary by location and that some cakes may only be available to order online.

    Sources indicate that when it comes to Thanksgiving, few people would argue with the idea that the holiday isn't complete without at least one pumpkin dessert. However, instead of serving the expected pie this year, opt for this cheesecake — in addition to a creamy base full of intense pumpkin flavor, the whole dessert is topped with pecans and a generous drizzle of caramel sauce.

    A two-pack of Ferrara's Bakery 8-inch Pumpkin Cheesecake with Caramel and Pecan Topping is available at Costco for $119.99.

    In a recent development, panettone is an Italian delicacy made from a yeasted dough studded with dried and candied fruit, and it has a lightly sweet flavor and fluffy texture. This bready cake is incredibly versatile and can be the foundation for many fall recipes. Try tearing it into pieces to make a delicious bread pudding, or follow Giada De Laurentiis's suggestion for leftover panettone and use it to top a holiday salad.

    Chiostro di Saronno Panettone Classico is available at Costco for $29.99.

    It has been revealed that whether you're starting your day with a cup of joe, pausing for a midafternoon pick-me-up, or finishing a meal with coffee or tea, this cake from Collin Street Bakery should be on the table. It comes in a beautiful white tin and includes a cup of icing for drizzling, while the warming cinnamon spice feels like a hug on your palate. It also makes a beautiful gift.

    Collin Street Bakery Cinnamon Coffee Cake is available at Costco for $34.99.

    In a recent development, collin Street Bakery is a Texas-based organization, and the Lone Star State is known for producing pecans, so you're almost guaranteed to have delicious pecan flavor in this pair of cakes. Besides containing the rich nuts, each one is chock-full of either pineapple or glacéed apricots. The batter for these cakes is also sweetened with honey.

    Collin Street Bakery Apricot & Pineapple Pecan Cake Bundle is available at Costco for $64.99.

    It has been revealed that for some, Christmas cannot arrive soon enough. Fortunately, Costco has a little preview of the holiday for these individuals in the form of this mini pecan cake bundle, which includes four favorite flavors: cherry fudge cake, pineapple cake, blonde cake, and a classic fruitcake. If you're wondering how fruitcakes can last all year, adding a heavy dose of alcohol can help preserve them.

    The Collin Street Bakery Mini Pecan Cake Bundle is available at Costco for $49.99.

    The Knipschildt brand once held the Guinness World Record for the most expensive chocolate truffle in the world, but you don't need to take out a loan to enjoy this dessert. This flourless cake features a layer of rich chocolate ganache and is finished with the chocolatier's signature truffles. It's a striking cake that will bring a bit of sophistication to your next gathering.

    Knipschildt Chocopologie Truffle Flourless Chocolate Cake is available at Costco for $69.99.

    Sources indicate that tiramisu may seem like tres leches, but it's an entirely different dessert. Its name translates to "lift me up," and while traditional versions may come in a square format, this one from Ferrara's Bakery is round and features an attractive collar of brown and white stripes. The bakery makes its own ladyfingers and douses them in coffee and coffee liqueur before layering them with sweetened mascarpone cheese.

    A two-pack of Ferrara's Bakery 8-inch Tiramisu Cake is available at Costco for $99.99.

    If you love the combination of chocolate and peanut butter, then this cake is for you. The base is made from a fudge brownie, and it's topped with layers of peanut butter mousse and decadent chocolate cake. As if that's not enough, the whole confection gets a crown of brownie pieces, chocolate fudge, and peanut butter chips.

    In a recent development, for the consummate chocolate lover, no other flavors should get in the way of a chocolate cake, and this one is nothing short of perfection. It starts with four layers of rich chocolate sponge sandwiching velvety milk chocolate mousse; then, the entire thing gets covered in chocolate ganache and a coating of chocolate shavings that resemble bark, making this cake look like an edible tree trunk. It's pre-sliced, too, ensuring that everyone gets a fair share.

    Recent findings suggest that sometimes simple is better, especially when you want to add your own personal touches to something, and this plain Jon Donaire cheesecake is a perfect example. Try drizzling it with dulce de leche and finishing it with chopped walnuts, or top it with apple pie filling and a sprinkling of mixed spices for an autumnal take on a classic. You can even cover it with poached pear halves.

    Jon Donaire 10-inch New York Cheesecake is available at Costco for $59.99.

    This carrot cake features thick layers of cake and cream cheese frosting and is covered with a generous coating of vanilla buttercream. For an elegant touch, it's topped with silk cherry blossoms, and comes in a striking box tied with a beautiful ribbon, too. If you're not a fan of nuts or raisins, this cake is free of both, so nothing gets in the way of the spiced carrot flavor.

    The Cake Bake Shop 8-inch Round Carrot Cake is available at Costco for $159.99.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (511 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    The Egg McMuffin Order You Can Only Find In Canada

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • McDonald's breakfast is a thing of beauty, and if you think we've got it good here in the States, you probably haven't seen what's sitting on Canada's breakfast menu.
    • The Egg BLT starts with McDonald's signature ring-shaped steamed (not fried) egg, paired with hickory-smoked bacon, crisp lettuce, and fresh tomato, then finished with a creamy, mayo-like sauce and a slice of cheese, all stacked on a toasted English muffin.
    • In a recent development, to get your hands on an Egg BLT McMuffin in the U.S., you'll have to get creative.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    McDonald's breakfast is a thing of beauty, and if you think we've got it good here in the States, you probably haven't seen what's sitting on Canada's breakfast menu. Alongside familiar faves, you'll find items Americans can't order, the most envy-inducing among them arguably being the Egg BLT McMuffin. Once you hear what's in it, don't be surprised if you catch yourself planning a trip to our northern neighbor.

    The Egg BLT starts with McDonald's signature ring-shaped steamed (not fried) egg, paired with hickory-smoked bacon, crisp lettuce, and fresh tomato, then finished with a creamy, mayo-like sauce and a slice of cheese, all stacked on a toasted English muffin. A second version uses nearly identical ingredients but swaps the whole leaves for shredded lettuce. You can only get this variation at McDonald's restaurants located inside Walmart stores — part of a decades-old partnership that once placed roughly 1,000 outposts in the retail chain. McDonald's later closed hundreds of them as drive-thrus became the main source of sales, though Walmart continues to host many locations in Canada.

    In a recent development, to get your hands on an Egg BLT McMuffin in the U.S., you'll have to get creative. Your best bet is to start with a Bacon, Egg & Cheese McMuffin, which already ticks off half the ingredients. Ask for a touch of mayo, which gets you close to the sauce of the Canadian original. Since lettuce and tomatoes are lunchtime items, your odds improve near the end of breakfast hours when stores are prepping the lunch menu — you'll likely have to order them at the counter or window.

    Industry observers note that the Egg BLT might have already convinced you to add McDonald's to your itinerary next time you're in Canada, but it's not the only breakfast item worth the detour. One that caught our eye was the Mighty McGriddles. While the U.S. offers the Bacon, Egg & Cheese and Sausage, Egg & Cheese varieties separately, the Canadian version puts both to shame by stacking a double helping of hickory-smoked bacon, a sausage patty, egg, and cheese between two maple-flavored griddle cakes — a gloriously overstuffed creation that lives up to its name. The Mighty McMuffin follows the same logic, coming loaded with both meats for anyone who can never decide between the two.

    Sources indicate that another familiar face on Canadian McDonald's breakfast menus is the bagel, though while America only offers plain, Canada also serves sesame and everything varieties. You can even order one toasted with butter or Philadelphia cream cheese — widely known as the best store-bought brand — as if you're at a proper bagel shop.

    Recent findings suggest that canada's McDonald's restaurants aren't afraid to put a twist on U.S. staples, and they also introduce new items altogether. You won't find chicken anywhere on the standard U.S. breakfast menu, which makes the Chicken McGriddles feel like a curveball up north. The simple yet delicious sandwich pairs a breaded chicken patty with two sweet, maple-flavored griddle cakes for some serious sweet-and-savory fusion.

    #10677. Latest Update: This Breakfast Addition Sharpens Memory Later In The Day

    📅 29 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (546 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Org ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: This Breakfast Addition Sharpens Memory Later In The Day

    📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.
    • A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.
    • Adding walnuts to breakfast could help people respond faster on mental tasks and learn information more effectively later in the day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.

    A simple breakfast addition improved reaction times, but its effects on memory took a more complicated turn.

    Adding walnuts to breakfast could help people respond faster on mental tasks and learn information more effectively later in the day.

    A generous handful produced small cognitive benefits over the following six hours, although memory performance varied with the timing of the tests.

    Walnuts may influence how the brain directs attention and obtains the energy needed for demanding mental work.

    Professor Claire Williams, study co-author, stated:.

    “A handful of walnuts with breakfast could give young adults a mental edge when they need to perform at the top of their game.”.

    The research involved over 30 healthy young adults aged 18–30, who ate two different breakfasts on separate visits to the laboratory.

    One contained 50 g of crushed walnuts mixed into muesli and vanilla yoghurt, while the other contained no nuts.

    The breakfasts contained almost identical calorie and fat totals, with butter added to the comparison meal to help achieve this match.

    Participants completed tests before breakfast and again two, four and six hours afterwards, while researchers also recorded their brain activity.

    After the walnut breakfast, participants responded faster on tasks involving attention, resisting distractions and switching between different mental rules.

    These abilities form part of executive function, which helps us control our responses and adapt to changing demands.

    The differences were modest, averaging around eight milliseconds on the attention test and 22 milliseconds when switching between rules.

    Whether improvements of this size would make a noticeable difference outside the laboratory remains uncertain.

    The memory findings were more complicated.

    Two hours after eating walnuts, participants performed slightly worse when repeatedly learning and recalling a list of words.

    By six hours, however, the pattern had reversed, with better performance after walnuts than after the comparison breakfast.

    One possibility is that walnuts helped protect learning performance as the testing day wore on.

    Repeated mental effort can make it harder to take in new information, so preserving the ability to learn could be useful even without improving every aspect of memory.

    However, participants did not report feeling less mentally fatigued after walnuts, leaving this explanation unconfirmed.

    Another possibility is that some benefits emerged gradually as nutrients were absorbed and processed.

    Walnuts contain omega-3 fats, protein and plant compounds called polyphenols, which could contribute individually or together.

    Electrical recordings revealed differences in frontal and parietal brain activity after the two breakfasts.

    These regions contribute to attention, memory and the control of behaviour.

    The changes may indicate that walnuts altered how mental resources were allocated during the tests, although they do not establish precisely why performance improved.

    Blood samples also revealed slightly higher glucose availability and lower concentrations of circulating free fatty acids after walnuts.

    Greater glucose availability might help fuel demanding mental work.

    The study was published in the journal Food & Function (Bell et al., 2025).

    Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean.

    #10673. 14 French Desserts You Should Try Once In Your Life

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2409 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    14 French Desserts You Should Try Once In Your Life

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2409 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • French cuisine is largely known for its decadent textures, flavors, and presentations, and this includes a long list of regional desserts.
    • If you aren't already familiar with French desserts, it doesn't matter if you are fluent in the language or not; the names of the country's culinary creations don't always alert you to what they actually are.
    • The tart Tatin may have a fancy name, but don't let that fool you.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    French cuisine is largely known for its decadent textures, flavors, and presentations, and this includes a long list of regional desserts. We all know about croissants, and, yes, when infused with the right sweet elements, they definitely count as a dessert, but that's just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to French desserts. In fact, there is a seemingly never-ending list of eye-catching sweet treats that hail from the country. The ones found below, though, are so mouthwateringly delicious that everyone should try them at least once in their lives.

    If you aren't already familiar with French desserts, it doesn't matter if you are fluent in the language or not; the names of the country's culinary creations don't always alert you to what they actually are. With this in mind, if you're interested in sampling a few — why wouldn't you be? — but aren't sure where to start, we can help point you in the right direction. So, get your fork and spoon ready, because once you learn about the collection of French desserts below, you'll be dying to get your hands on them.

    The tart Tatin may have a fancy name, but don't let that fool you. It is actually akin to an apple pie, just flipped upside down — and there's nothing extravagant about that. The French version of the dessert also has humble origins. As the story goes, in the late 1800s, Caroline (of Caroline and Stephanie Tatin's Inn, located south of Paris) forgot to put a crust on the bottom of her apple pie. Due to being exceptionally busy, she decided to put it on top instead and see what would happen. When she took it out of the oven and flipped it over, she saw that her misstep led to a happy result: The apples were beautifully caramelized. When she served it to the inn's guests, it was an immediate success, and the tarte Tatin was officially born.

    Creating a tart Tatin is fairly accessible to novice home cooks. It only calls for five ingredients: apples, flour, butter, eggs, and sugar. The trickiest part is arranging the slices of fruit in a decorative way on the bottom of the pan. Actually, despite her massive culinary repertoire, Ina Garten admits it is the recipe she makes most because it is not only delicious, but easy to create, as well. If it's good enough for Garten to come back time and time again, you'd better believe it's a French dessert everyone should give a go at least once.

    Crème brûlée is one of the most easily recognizable and widely popular French desserts in the United States, but, interestingly enough, its origins are somewhat disputed. France, England, and Spain all claim to be the birthplace of the dessert. Regardless, since its invention, wherever that happened to be, there's no doubt it has fully integrated itself into traditional French cuisine, and if you've never had the joy of eating one before, you are truly missing out.

    It has been revealed that in its most basic format, crème brûlée is made with just four ingredients: egg yolks, sugar, heavy cream, and vanilla bean. While simple, the elements come together to form a creamy, custardy delight. Then, the top is scorched to form a layer of burnt sugar that's to die for. Topping it with a couple of fresh berries is also customary, but either way, it is simplicity at its finest. In fact, this is one case where the sum is much greater than its parts. In addition to the sweet, rich flavor of the custard itself, part of the fun of eating one is using a spoon to crack the burnt layer on top. It not only adds a caramelized taste but contributes textural variation, and that is always a plus. Whether you decide to try your hand at making crème brûlée yourself or choose to seek it out from a restaurant, it's a French dessert that's worth your attention.

    Éclairs have been around since the 1860s, and today, they are one of the more popular French desserts found in the United States. For good reason, too; they are tasty enough to go down in a flash. Speaking of which, the word directly translates to lightning.

    Name and popularity aside, éclairs are made with choux pastry, which is similar to doughnut pastry, but devoid of baking soda, baking powder, and yeast, and relies on steam to rise. As a result, after being formed into long cylindrical pieces, the dough cooks up to be exceptionally light and airy. That's just the start of the legendary éclair, though. They are also filled with pastry cream or custard and then topped with either fondant or ganache icing — both of which are harder styles of icing, so you can still feel free to enjoy éclairs with your hands.

    Recent findings suggest that arguably, the most popular flavor of éclair is chocolate, but thanks to the versatility of the choux pastry shell, they are welcoming to a world of other flavors as well. Everything from caramel to pistachio to Nutella to strawberry to matcha with chocolate and beyond can be found enhancing the delightful little pastry.

    French yogurt cake, or gâteaux au yaourt in the native language, is another easy yet extremely satisfying dessert that deserves some time in the spotlight. In France, it is a popular recipe for kids to learn, likely because of the simple recipe, which calls for three eggs, one part oil, one part yogurt, two parts sugar, three parts flour, and leavening. Even so, when it comes out of the oven, you have a drool-worthy, slightly tangy cake that is moister than pound cake (if you can fathom that) while still presenting a delicate crumb.

    In a recent development, since French yogurt cake is not a common restaurant offering, if you want to give it a taste, you'll likely have to make one yourself. Or, at the very least, enlist a friend to do it — um, mom? Thankfully, though, it is one of the more straightforward must-try French desserts out there, so it should be attainable for even the most novice home cooks. The simplicity of the French yogurt cake also makes it prime for a plethora of flavor infusions. So, if you want to add citrus, or brandy, or fruit to the mix, go right ahead.

    It has been revealed that crêpes are a delicately thin pancake-like creation that's ready and waiting for a world of flavor and ingredient infusions. Still, a Crêpes Suzette is quite possibly the most delicious and famous version of them all. It consists of classic crêpes in a sauce made of sugar, orange juice, and an orange liqueur, like Gran Marnier. The entire thing is also smothered in brandy and set on fire, which leads to a caramelized, citrusy, sweet flambé sauce that will draw just about anyone in. Heck, even watching a chef prepare one catches the eye, and that's why it's often done in full view when ordered in a restaurant.

    Interestingly enough, crêpes Suzette is another iconic French dessert that was first created by accident — and this particular story is not disputed. In 1895, Henri Carpentier, a 14-year-old assistant waiter at the Maitre at Monte Carlo's Cafe Paris, was preparing dessert for the Prince of Wales (who'd later become King Edward VII of England). While doing so, he accidentally caught the cordials he was working with on fire, and instead of becoming flustered and starting over from scratch, he tasted the sauce and realized he'd come up with something extraordinary.

    Industry observers note that don't let the flambé scare you too much if you want to try creating one at home; it truly does lead to exceptional flavor. However, you can still make a tasty rendition sans the potential fire hazard; it just won't be quite as authentic.

    Recent findings suggest that first and foremost, Mont Blanc is known for being the highest mountain in the Alps. However, for those in the know, it is also a delectable French sweet treat with Alpine-inspired appeal. In fact, when created, the Mont Blanc dessert resembles a snow-capped mountain peak, so the name is more than fitting. The exact origins of it is uncertain, but a reigning theory is that it was developed in Paris, France, in the 19th century. During that era, chestnuts started to grow in popularity in the region, and people began incorporating them into sweet dishes, instead of the customary savory ones.

    The main components of a Mont Blanc dessert are as follows: It starts with a crisp meringue base, which is topped with thin strands of chestnut purée, and then finished off with a pile of whipped cream. Traditionally, a vermicelli tip is used to pipe the chestnut puree, but other shapes are also common. Either way, though, the yummy chestnut puree is the star of the show, offering a nutty, rich flavor that offsets the creamy whipped cream and meringue in a delightful way.

    Hailing from the Basque region in southwest France, the Gâteau Basque became widely popular in the 19th century. Its growth in the culinary scene is largely attributed to a particular baker, Marianne Hirigoyen, who first sold them in local markets before opening a brick-and-mortar bakery. Since then, the gâteau Basque's acceptance into French culinary tradition has been more than cemented. Actually, fast-forward to today, and there's now a museum and a two-day festival in October dedicated to the dessert. If that doesn't tell you exactly why it is a must-try French recipe, we don't know what would.

    Whether you call them canelé, cannelé de Bordeaux, or canelé Bordelais, these yummy little French pastries are time-consuming to make — the dough needs to rest for up to 24 hours before baking. Even so, their delectable mix of textures and delicious buttery, custard-y flavors are worth the effort used to make them and then some.

    Recent findings suggest that small and cylindrical with fluted edges, the center of canelés are made with flour, milk, sugar, butter, vanilla bean, eggs, salt, and rum. Once mixed with care, the dough rests for an extended time before baking in copper molds. After they're cooked, a delicious coating of edible beeswax and butter fills the molds and is also poured over the top before baking again. When that's done, you're left with delicious bite-sized (well, almost) custard-filled cakes featuring a caramelized crust on the exterior. Considering miniature copper fluted molds are not a customary tool in most homes, canelés aren't the first dessert we recommend trying to make at home. However, if you ever see them in a French bakery or restaurant, you'd be a fool not to give them a try.

    Recent findings suggest that opera cake is one of the coffee desserts that are always worth ordering, and guess what? It's also a French dessert everyone should try at least once. That is, of course, if you know what's good for you — and in this case, we truly hope you do.

    Created by Cyrique Gavillon, the opera cake is just as much a thing of beauty as it is a delectable flavor wonderland. A rectangular-shaped cake at heart, it is made with alternating layers of coffee syrup-soaked almond cake, buttercream, and ganache, and then topped with a rich dark chocolate icing. Once completed, it not only looks stunning, but provides your palate with a mix of nutty, chocolatey, creamy, rich, coffee flavors that are hard to beat. Yes, it sounds a whole lot like tiramisu when the elements are taken at face value, but it is a delightful dessert all its own when it comes to how the ingredients come together. Plus, it's French, not Italian. Just saying.

    While simple to make, the Île flottante presents itself as an elegant dish, and as such, is a mainstay in French cuisine. In fact, while it's said French people prefer to purchase dessert from a local bakery, it is one recipe many natives still have in their repertoire. It just so happened to be Julia Child's favorite old-school dessert, as well. Since she is credited with bringing French cuisine to the United States and helping it grow in popularity, following her lead regarding the greatest culinary hits of the country just makes sense.

    According to recent reports, similar to éclairs, which we've already discussed, profiteroles are made with hollowed-out choux pastry, filled with custard or cream, and topped with icing. What sets them apart is their shape. Instead of being long and cylindrical, profiteroles are formed into small bite-sized balls. As a result, they are the perfect sweet treat for bringing to a gathering or munching on if you simply want a few bites. However, once you get a taste of their scrumptious textures and flavors, trying to eat just one will be quite a complicated task.

    Again, like éclairs, the most common icing flavor for profiteroles is chocolate. Still, they come in a myriad of other flavors, as well, so they have what it takes to pique the interest of many. For example, if chocolate is too one-dimensional for you — we are judging you — you can also make chocolate hazelnut profiteroles, vanilla ones, or just about any other flavor you can dream up.

    It has been revealed that last but certainly not least on our list of French desserts you need to try is clafoutis. The name may sound posh, but it's actually another sweet treat that's incredibly easy to make, so you don't have to be an established French baker to create one at home. Plus, it may be a dessert, but it is also acceptable to eat it for breakfast. Okay, now we are really listening.

    In a recent development, clafoutis consists of fruit smothered with a thick custard made from sugar, flour, milk, and eggs. The texture is akin to flan, but undeniably has all the French flair a Francophile could want. Most traditionally, cherries create the meaty fruit of clafoutis, but other berries and fruits, like raspberries, are also commonly used to pull off the recipe. While not necessarily a dessert, if you want to go in a savory direction, fruit can also be substituted for prosciutto, cheese, and tomatoes, so think of it like a choose-your-own-adventure type dish. No matter how you build it, though, clafoutis is one French creation that deserves more recognition, at least in the States.

    #10671. Tech Report: Forget Butter Or Mayo: Spread This Rich Ingredient On Bread For Heartier Grilled Cheese

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (452 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Forget Butter Or Mayo: Spread This Rich Ingredient On Bread For Heartier Grilled Cheese

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (452 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A grilled cheese is already plenty hearty, but the common tip of using cured meats to increase its satisfying flavor — like in this tasty maple bacon variation — may interfere with your filling's texture if you prefer a smooth, gooey filling.
    • Duck fat is one of the most prized cooking fats in the culinary world because it has a higher smoke point than butter (around 375 degrees Fahrenheit) and a beautifully silky texture rich in subtle, meaty flavors.
    • Using duck fat on grilled cheese is pretty easy, but there are a few tricks that can really maximize your results.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A grilled cheese is already plenty hearty, but the common tip of using cured meats to increase its satisfying flavor — like in this tasty maple bacon variation — may interfere with your filling's texture if you prefer a smooth, gooey filling. Duck fat is the perfect way around this because it adds meatiness without changing any other ingredients, enriching the bread with umami with just a single smear.

    Duck fat is one of the most prized cooking fats in the culinary world because it has a higher smoke point than butter (around 375 degrees Fahrenheit) and a beautifully silky texture rich in subtle, meaty flavors. Just like spreading it on burger buns, using duck fat on grilled cheese can give you crispier bread because you can cook it at a higher temperature. When left at room temperature, it has a consistency similar to softened butter, making it easy to spread or drop in a pan, depending on your preference. Its unique composition of fats and subtle meaty flavor mean you'll notice its richness even in small amounts. Though it has a touch of gaminess, it's quite subtle and serves to elevate creamy and aged cheeses alike with an added layer of complexity.

    Using duck fat on grilled cheese is pretty easy, but there are a few tricks that can really maximize your results. Blending it with another fat, using it for some added seasoning, and picking the right pan can all give you the perfect sandwich.

    Recent findings suggest that mixing a fat with a high smoke point with one that burns more easily is a simple way to combine the best of both worlds. The richness of butter is irreplaceable, but you can incorporate some of duck fat's higher-heat cooking properties by swirling the two together before spreading the mix on your bread. Similarly, you can also bring your duck fat to a low, gentle simmer and add herbs and aromatics to flavor it beforehand. Whether you do this when rendering the fat yourself or just for a few minutes before adding your sandwich, a bit of sage can lend tremendous depth, while a smashed clove of garlic can mimic the rich flavor of toum.

    It has been revealed that while a nonstick pan is great for butter since it doesn't retain as much heat, you might want to go in the opposite direction for duck fat. A heavy cast iron or stainless steel skillet helps prevent the surface temperature from dropping when you add the sandwich, maintaining that lovely heat that makes duck fat work so well. Plus, animal fats are great for cast iron's seasoning, helping you maintain your pan's coating while you cook!

    #10668. Add This Crunchy Ingredient To Ground Beef For Lighter Steakhouse Burgers (Hint: It's Not Breadcrumbs)

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (481 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Add This Crunchy Ingredient To Ground Beef For Lighter Steakhouse Burgers (Hint: It's Not Breadcrumbs)

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (481 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
    • Sources indicate that the actual difference between a hamburger and a steakburger comes down to the quality of meat used in the grind, but the difference between a homemade steakburger and one from a steakhouse is all about a lighter texture.
    • Industry observers note that "Any kind of cracker or breadcrumbs will make a burger lighter," Clark notes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Sources indicate that the actual difference between a hamburger and a steakburger comes down to the quality of meat used in the grind, but the difference between a homemade steakburger and one from a steakhouse is all about a lighter texture. Melissa Clark, author of "The Big Book of Dinner: Recipes and Rules (and How to Break Them)," tells us that achieving that characteristic is quite easy if you use ground cracker crumbs.

    Industry observers note that "Any kind of cracker or breadcrumbs will make a burger lighter," Clark notes. "Ritz and saltines work really well. They are very airy, which helps lighten the ground meat." Beef is rather dense, even if you avoid overworking it into a firm, puck-like consistency that's more similar to sausage than a tender patty. But a quarter cup of ground crackers per pound of meat can make a world of difference.

    When meat cooks, it contracts and releases juice and fat. Crackers, however, absorb them rather than allowing them to seep out of the patty, preventing it from shriveling up too much. Since steakhouse burgers typically use thick patties, this also keeps them nice and moist. Whereas a thin sliver of well-crusted beef may be just what you want in a smashburger, retaining moisture is a vital component to keeping your steakhouse burgers not only light, but also at their peak flavor.

    Industry observers note that using plain, unsalted crackers can still keep your steakhouse burgers light, but it would be a missed opportunity for better flavor. While you also don't want to use something starch-free, like a nut- or seed-based variety, Melissa Clark is a significant believer in picking a tasty brand and smashing them up properly.

    In a recent development, "Using crackers can add great flavor – Ritz, with their butteriness, are especially lovely," Clark explains. Flavorful but unobtrusive, Ritz crackers are the perfect addition to any savory dish because just about everything can benefit from their toasty richness. But if you want to get a bit experimental, you can also just as easily use Cheez-Its or anything seasoned. This is an easy way to avoid coming up with a specialty spice blend since you'll be adding enough to thoroughly flavor your meat.

    According to recent reports, clark is also a proponent of using whatever method you can to grind the crackers into a fine powder. "Grind the crackers in a food processor, blender or tuck them in a plastic bag and crush them under a rolling pin," she added. Large chunks can make some bites unexpectedly soggy and, if using a seasoned cracker, a little too flavorful. Plus, if some parts of your blend don't have a starch, they may end up expressing their juices too much, leaving some bites juicy and light and others dense and dry.

    What Happier People Tend To Believe About Others

    📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (644 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.
    • A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.
    • Trusting others is linked to greater happiness and life satisfaction, a review involving over 2.5 million people finds.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.

    A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.

    Trusting others is linked to greater happiness and life satisfaction, a review involving over 2.5 million people finds.

    Happier people also tend to become more trusting over time.

    The link between trust and happiness is slightly stronger in children, adolescents and older adults, possibly because supportive relationships are especially key at these ages.

    Trust may help meet the need to belong by making it easier to build relationships in which people feel supported and secure.

    The research combined almost 1,000 findings from studies involving people aged six to 84.

    The analysis examined how trust related to everyday emotions, including happiness and sadness, as well as people’s overall satisfaction with their lives.

    Greater trust was consistently associated with better wellbeing.

    The association was somewhat stronger among children and adolescents than among young and middle-aged adults, and stronger among older adults than young adults.

    Trust may matter more at ages when people are building close relationships or becoming more dependent on others.

    For younger people, learning whom to trust is part of building meaningful friendships and supportive social networks.

    In later life, people may prioritise a smaller circle of close relationships and depend more on others for support.

    The researchers distinguished between trust in familiar people, trust in people generally and trust in institutions.

    The first involves confidence in someone known personally, such as a partner, friend or relative.

    General trust involves expectations about people more broadly, including strangers, while institutional trust concerns organisations such as governments, banks and the police.

    All three were associated with better wellbeing, but trust in familiar people indicated the strongest connection.

    Trust may support wellbeing partly because close relationships require a willingness to be vulnerable.

    Expecting someone to respond with care can make it easier to seek help, cooperate and maintain a supportive connection.

    These relationships may satisfy the basic psychological need to feel connected to others and cared for in return.

    Trust could also provide a broader sense of security and predictability, making the social world feel more dependable.

    This may help explain why trust was slightly more closely related to overall life satisfaction than to positive or negative emotions.

    Life satisfaction reflects a broader assessment of how life is going, whereas emotions can fluctuate with immediate experiences.

    The relationship also worked in the other direction, with greater wellbeing predicting more trust later.

    One proposed explanation is that emotions influence how people interpret the world around them.

    Feeling happy may encourage more positive perceptions of other people, while anxiety may draw attention towards threats and uncertainty.

    Trust and wellbeing could therefore reinforce each other, with supportive expectations helping people feel better and positive feelings making trust easier.

    The wider social environment mattered too, with a stronger connection between trust and wellbeing in countries where people were generally more trusting.

    A trusting outlook may be more beneficial when the people around us are dependable.

    Simply encouraging someone to trust more overlooks the behaviour of the people and institutions receiving that trust.

    Professor Catrin Finkenauer, study co-author, noted:.

    “But trust can’t be forced—it has to be earned.”.

    The findings therefore highlight the importance of honesty, reliability, transparency and fair treatment in relationships and institutions.

    “When we build trust, we also support mental health and stronger communities.”.

    The study was published in the journal Psychological Bulletin (Bi et al., 2025).
